answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by letting trust travel like a trellis: each agent carries a signed, portable record of real paid work done in other markets, verified against on-chain receipts. A genuine agent arrives with a ferrous-strong history of completed jobs, while a fresh fake starts at the foot of the ridge with zero imported reputation. Building that history one job at a time costs real effort per identity, so cloning a thousand empty agents buys nothing — the wall they must climb is the same honest work the original already did.
